Assembly 0.7.1

New: Resync Selected Clips. Sound rolls you bring in yourself with Field Recorder guide tracks can sit a little off the reference. Select the reference clip and the roll clips under it, then choose Session ▸ Resync Selected Clips…, or Resync in the Match button. Assembly measures each take against the reference by its audio and puts it back in sync, to the sample.

  • Clips stay where they are. Each roll clip is replaced at the same position and length, playing from the right place in its roll, so its edges stay on the picture cuts.
  • A summary comes first. It says how far out each take is and what will change before anything is written. Edit ▸ Undo in Pro Tools takes it back.
  • Takes with fades are left alone for now, and the summary says so.
  • New clips are named and colored the way Assemble names and colors them. Clip gain on the old clips isn't kept.

Assembling:

  • Placement is exact in more cases. A sync measurement could read one sample early, which could put a short clip a sample out. It no longer does.
  • A selection that starts just after a crossfade now places its first clip at the true edit, not the middle of the fade.
  • A clip that follows a crossfade keeps its exact end, and its fade out when you recreate fades.

Also: Help now lists what's new in each version, under Settings, Reports and Updates.

Updating from before 0.7? Assembly now uses projects: the first time it opens, it asks to move your deep scan into one. Help ▸ Settings, Reports and Updates ▸ What's new lists what every version brought.

Assembly 0.7

Assembly now uses projects. The first time you open this version, it asks to move your deep scan into a project. Nothing is scanned again, and your sound rolls aren't touched.

Why it has to move:

  • Each show remembers its own. A project holds a show's deep scan, track names, colors and options in one file. Changing shows no longer means swapping the database and setting everything again.
  • Open it like any other file. Double-click a project, or use File ▸ Open Project… or Open Recent.
  • Several at once. Each project has its own window. They take turns with Pro Tools, and say so when one has to wait.

Before you update:

  • You can keep the old database as a backup. It's ticked whenever the drive has room. On an exFAT drive it uses as much space as the deep scan, and copying a large one takes a while.
  • Older versions of Assembly can't open projects, so it's best if everyone on a show moves together.
  • Connect the drive with your deep scan first. If it isn't connected, Assembly says so and asks again once it's back.

Also new:

  • Options save themselves. There's no Save: any option or color you change is in the project straight away, and a new project starts from the options you used last.
  • The wrong project is caught. If a session was last used in another project, Assembly says so before Match or Align.
  • A project links to its script and never holds a copy, so passing a project on doesn't pass the script with it.
  • Scan Sound Rolls is now ⇧⌘O. ⌘O is Open Project. Open Database and Choose New Database Location have gone: a deep scan lives in its project.
  • A new project goes in its rolls folder unless you choose somewhere else, so it travels with the rolls.
  • The probes in the Diagnostics menu are out of the way. Open the menu and hold Option to see them.

Help has a new page, Moving to Projects, with all of this in more detail.

Assembly 0.6.9

The toolbar:

  • Every button now has its name under it: Match, Align, Scene/Shot, Diagnostic and Help. Match and Scene/Shot are new, and drop down with their commands.
  • Connecting to Pro Tools has moved. Connect and Disconnect are in the Match button now, and step 2 always says whether Assembly is connected, even before a scan.

Assembling:

  • Tracks can go in a folder. A new option in the Tracks card puts an assembly's tracks in a folder track named for your prefix, such as ASM Assembly. It is off until you turn it on.
  • Stop finishes the step it is on, then stops. It used to report a connection failure at that step.
  • The custom track color no longer comes up empty. If Pro Tools does not give Assembly its palette, the picker now says so and tries again each time it opens.

Aligning:

  • The progress window says Aligning rather than Assembling.
